tools.description:
Wait for Alloy's answers to ``ask_alloy`` questions that are still working.

Pass every conversation you are waiting on: ``waiting_on`` from your latest
Alloy reply. Waits up to ``wait_seconds`` and returns as soon as any has an
answer you have not received, with every such answer in ``answers``, each
with its ``question``, in the ``ask_alloy`` shape. If none is ready in time,
``answers`` is empty and ``still_working`` says what Alloy is doing. Call
again with the new ``waiting_on`` until it is empty; if you reply to the
user first, say Alloy is still answering. When nothing is owed, it repeats
each conversation's newest answer marked ``already_returned``: you have it
already. Conversations that are not yours or do not exist are listed in
``not_found``, and ``message`` says what to do next. Set ``finish_now``
when the user wants answers sooner: Alloy starts no new work and answers
from what it has gathered, so answers may be less complete.

```ts
mcp__Alloy__ask_alloy_result(args: {
// Explain why you are calling this tool and how it fits into the user's overall goal. This parameter is used for analytics and user intent tracking. YOU MUST provide 15-25 words (count carefully). NEVER use first person ('I', 'we', 'you') - maintain third-person perspective. NEVER include sensitive information such as credentials, passwords, or personal data. Example (20 words): "Searching across the organization's repositories to find all open issues related to performance complaints and latency issues for team prioritization."
context: string,
// One conversation, as a one-item ``conversation_ids``.
conversation_id?: string | null, // default: null
// The conversations to wait on, from ``waiting_on``.
conversation_ids?: string[] | null, // default: null
// Ask Alloy to answer now from what it has.
finish_now?: boolean, // default: false
// How long to wait (default 30, max 45).
wait_seconds?: integer, // default: 30
}): Promise<{ [key: string]: any }>;
```

tools.description:
List Iceberg table names in the org's Storage, or search columns.

Discovery is filtered and paginated because an organization can have more
than 1,000 tables.

- `name_filter`: case-insensitive substring on the table name, e.g.
  `name_filter="battery"` returns every `*battery*` table.
- `column_filter`: case-insensitive substring searched across the field
  names of recorded topics. For example, `column_filter="heading"`
  returns `{schema, table, column, matched_fields, topic, schema_hashes}`
  rows like `fleet, gps__fix, data, ["heading_deg"]`: one per table, or
  one per topic when the org keeps every topic in `mesh.messages`.
  Matched fields sit in the `data` struct; select them double-quoted
  (`data."heading_deg"`). When `coverage.status` is `partial`, some
  tables were not searched (for example older or non-recording uploads);
  find those with `name_filter`. `name_filter` and `column_filter` can be
  combined.
- `limit` (default 25, max 1000) + `offset` page the results; when more
  tables remain, the response includes `next_offset`.

Field names come from recorded message definitions, not the SQL schema.
Confirm the exact columns and types with `describe_mesh_table` before
writing SQL.

```ts
mcp__Alloy__list_mesh_tables(args: {
// Optional case-insensitive substring to match table names.
name_filter?: string | null, // default: null
// Optional case-insensitive substring to match field
// names in recorded topics.
column_filter?: string | null, // default: null
// Max tables per page (default 25, capped at 1000).
limit?: integer, // default: 25
// Pagination offset; pair with a returned `next_offset`.
offset?: integer, // default: 0
// Explain why you are calling this tool and how it fits into the user's overall goal. This parameter is used for analytics and user intent tracking. YOU MUST provide 15-25 words (count carefully). NEVER use first person ('I', 'we', 'you') - maintain third-person perspective. NEVER include sensitive information such as credentials, passwords, or personal data. Example (20 words): "Searching across the organization's repositories to find all open issues related to performance complaints and latency issues for team prioritization."
context: string,
}): Promise<{ [key: string]: any }>;
```

tools.description:
Run read-only DataFusion SQL over the org's Storage Iceberg tables.

Storage SQL uses fully qualified `alloy.*` Iceberg tables and supports
read-only SELECT and WITH queries. It is not DuckDB MCAP SQL; forms such as
`$FILE` and `read_mcap_*` functions are unsupported. Results are bounded by
`limit` and `offset`, including SQL without a LIMIT clause.

source_registry orgs have no per-topic `alloy.fleet.*` tables: read
telemetry from `alloy.mesh.messages` with an equality filter on `topic`,
fields as `data.<leaf>`. `schema_hash` is optional: without it the query
runs on the topic's hashes that have every column referenced (file and
metadata filters narrow them first); a column whose type differs between
them fails with the hashes to pick with `AND schema_hash = '...'` (hashes
in `alloy.mesh.schemas`).

Mission, exact `file_id`, and time-range predicates can reduce fleet scans
before aggregates, sorts, list expansion, or payload retrieval. A natural
metadata join on `file_id` (`alloy.mesh.file_meta`, or `alloy.mesh.metadata`
for source_registry orgs) can dynamically prune fleet files.
Supported top-level and primitive struct-leaf predicates can prune files
when metrics exist. Struct containers, list or map descendants, and pointer
payloads cannot prune files. The result `limit` bounds output, not scan or
blocking-operator work.

List indexes are 1-based. Bracket access after a list-of-struct index has
the form `data.points[1]['x']`. Full list expansion has the form
`CROSS JOIN UNNEST(t.data.items) AS u(item)`. Correlated expansion is inner,
accepts one list expression, and requires an alias. Null and empty lists
produce no rows. Correlated `JOIN UNNEST ... ON`, outer expansion,
`WITH ORDINALITY`, multi-argument correlated UNNEST, and arbitrary
correlated LATERAL subqueries are unsupported. Ordinary table joins remain
supported.

Supported large binary leaves such as `data.data` or `data.image.data` may
be pointer-backed. Project the exact leaf after selective inline filters;
`SELECT *` or the parent struct does not request nested payload hydration.
Pointer-backed payload contents are not filterable.

Engine validation, syntax, unsupported-form, and scan-budget failures are
returned in `error`. Transport and Arrow-stream failures can be transient
or can represent a late query/data error after streaming begins. A
selective query can be retried once after a transport or stream failure;
repeated failures require a narrower or simpler query.

```ts
mcp__Alloy__query_storage(args: {
// A SELECT query.
sql: string,
// Max rows to return (default 25, capped at 1000).
limit?: integer, // default: 25
// Pagination offset from a truncated response's `next_offset`.
offset?: integer, // default: 0
// When true, execute the same query twice at limit=1 and
// limit=5 and return measured response byte sizes instead of CSV rows.
// This estimates output size, not query scan or execution cost.
estimate_only?: boolean, // default: false
// Explain why you are calling this tool and how it fits into the user's overall goal. This parameter is used for analytics and user intent tracking. YOU MUST provide 15-25 words (count carefully). NEVER use first person ('I', 'we', 'you') - maintain third-person perspective. NEVER include sensitive information such as credentials, passwords, or personal data. Example (20 words): "Searching across the organization's repositories to find all open issues related to performance complaints and latency issues for team prioritization."
context: string,
}): Promise<{ [key: string]: any }>;
```

tools.description:
✅ PRIMARY TOOL for all location searches. Handles brand + location combinations automatically.

What this returns: Service locations matching your criteria, sorted by distance when location provided.

PARAMETERS:
- brand_name (optional): Human-readable brand like "Honda", "Tire and Wheel", "Glass Repair", "Rent a Car", "General Repair", "Collision Repair"
- latitude/longitude (optional): Search center coordinates
- service (optional): The service the user asked for, like "Oil Change", spelled as the services list spells it
- brand_name and coordinates are both optional, but provide at least one

SEARCH MODES (automatically determined):
1. Brand + Location → Up to 20 nearest locations for that brand (most common)
2. Location only → Up to 20 nearest locations of all brands
3. Location + service → Up to 20 nearest locations whose business type offers that service
4. Brand only → Up to 20 locations for that brand nationwide, not necessarily the closest ones (rarely needed; ask for the user's location instead when you can)

The service parameter narrows mode 2 into mode 3. It is ignored when brand_name is given, because a brand already names what the location does.

LOCATION HANDLING:
- If user specifies a location (city, address, "near X"), geocode it to lat/lng
- If user says "near me" or doesn't specify location, USE THE USER'S KNOWN COORDINATES
- Always default to user's current/known location when available

EXAMPLES:
- "Find Honda locations near me" → brand_name="Honda" + user's coordinates
- "Tire shop in Brooklyn" → brand_name="Tire and Wheel" + Brooklyn coordinates
- "Glass repair Charlottesville" → brand_name="Glass Repair" + Charlottesville coordinates
- "Auto repair shop in Tulsa" → brand_name="General Repair" + Tulsa coordinates
- "Body shop in Reno" → brand_name="Collision Repair" + Reno coordinates
- "Locations near me" → just coordinates (no brand)
- "Who can do an oil change near me?" → coordinates + service="Oil Change"
- "All Toyota locations" → brand_name="Toyota" only (nationwide, capped at 20; ask where the user is instead when you can)

SPECIALTY SERVICES (use brand_name):
- Tires/wheels → brand_name="Tire and Wheel"
- Auto glass → brand_name="Glass Repair"
- Car rental → brand_name="Rent a Car"
- General repair → brand_name="General Repair"
- Collision/body shop → brand_name="Collision Repair"

UNIVERSAL SERVICES (no brand needed):
- Oil change, brake service, car maintenance → location, plus service="Oil Change" or the matching name
- Sending the service narrows the results to business types that offer it. Location alone returns every nearby location that takes general service work, which is the old behaviour and still valid.

Each result includes:
- booking.next_tool: The tool to call next for this location. Call that tool, do not infer one from the brand name
- booking.flow: appointment, rental, quote_form, or none
- booking.agent_ready: this account's own agent-booking setting. Do not route on it. booking.next_tool is the routing answer and already accounts for it, so a location reporting false can still name a scraper tool
- business_category: Type of business
- services: Array of services offered
- booking.map_url: URL to book a service appointment online (rendered as the "Book Online" link). Use this one for any link shown to the user.
- booking.schedule_service_url: the raw entry URL get_availability/book_appointment drive directly. Never print this as a clickable link when booking.map_url is present; the rendered list falls back to it only when booking.map_url is null.

Returns: Service locations as a formatted list with names, addresses, and booking links. locations is capped at 20 even when more exist; total_count in the structured response says how many there actually were. If total_count is higher than the number of locations returned, tell the user the list is partial and offer to narrow by location. The overflow only happens on a brand-only nationwide search, where service is already ignored, so service cannot narrow it.

```ts
mcp__AutoMotion__find_locations(args: {
// Human-readable brand name like "Honda", "Toyota", "Tire and Wheel", "Glass Repair", "Rent a Car", "General Repair", "Collision Repair". Case-insensitive. If misspelled, you'll get suggestions.
brand_name?: string,
// Search center latitude (-90 to 90). Required for proximity search.
latitude?: number, // minimum: -90.0, maximum: 90.0
// Search center longitude (-180 to 180). Required for proximity search.
longitude?: number, // minimum: -180.0, maximum: 180.0
// Optional service the user needs, like "Oil Change" or "Full Windshield Replacement". Use a service name exactly as it appears in a location's services list or in the data://taxonomy/category-services.json resource. Narrows a proximity search without brand_name to locations whose category offers that service. Ignored when brand_name is given.
service?: string, // minLength: 1
}): Promise<{ locations: { name?: string | null, address: { street?: string | null, city?: string | null, state?: string | null, zip?: string | null, full: string }, coordinates: { latitude: number, longitude: number }, contact: { email?: string | null }, booking: { schedule_service_url?: string | null, map_url?: string | null, form_type: string | null, flow: string, agent_ready: boolean, next_tool: string }, account_id: string, brands?: { id: string, name?: string | null, logo?: string | null, logo_url?: string | null, booking_form_type?: string | null }[], business_category?: string | null, services: string[] }[], total_count: number, searchedBrand: { id: string, name?: string | null, logo: string | null } | null, search_center?: { latitude: number, longitude: number }, attribution: { source: string, medium: string, campaign: string } }>;
```

tools.description:
Use this when: User wants to book an appointment or get contact details for a specific location from search results.

⚠️ CRITICAL LIMITATIONS:
This tool returns ONLY contact information and booking URL. It does NOT provide:
- Appointment availability or scheduling details
- Service center hours or wait times
- Pricing, service quality, or reviews
- Operational details about this specific location
- Any information beyond basic contact details

DO NOT make recommendations about:
- Best time to book appointments
- Service quality or reliability
- Location practices or upselling patterns
- Wait times or service speed

What this ACTUALLY returns:
- Booking URL (map_url, for user to schedule directly; show this one, not booking_url)
- Email and address, plus a phone number when the location has no booking URL
- List of brands/products the location carries

When to use:
- ✅ User needs booking URL or contact info for a specific location
- ✅ User asks "How do I contact this location?"

When NOT to use:
- ❌ User asks about hours, availability, pricing, wait times → Tell them to use booking URL or contact via email
- ❌ Searching for locations → Use find_locations instead

After calling this tool: Provide ONLY the contact info returned, and offer only the fields that came back. map_url, booking_url, the contact email and the contact phone are all nullable. Show the user map_url for scheduling questions, falling back to booking_url only when map_url is null; never show booking_url when map_url is present. When neither URL is present, offer whichever contact channels came back: a phone number is returned only in that case, alongside the email, and either can be null. When nothing came back, say the location returned no way to reach it instead of inventing a link or an address.

account_id: string, // format: "uuid"

tools.description:
List the rental vehicle classes available at a rental location, with prices. Call after find_locations once the user has chosen a rental location.

Read-only: this reserves nothing and books nothing, so it is safe to repeat.

Not free, though: every call drives a live headless-browser scrape and the scraper runs a single worker, so calls queue behind each other and behind any booking in progress. Compare two or three locations at most, one at a time, and prefer the locations find_locations already ranked over sweeping the list.

Call this when the user wants to choose a vehicle class or see prices. book_rental takes vehicle_class as an optional argument and picks the first available class when it is omitted, so this call is not a prerequisite for booking.

When to use:
- The user picked a car rental location and wants to know what vehicles or prices are available
- You need a valid vehicle_class value before calling book_rental

When NOT to use:
- For service or repair appointments, use get_availability instead. This tool serves rental brands only
- Before find_locations, since you need a valid account_id first
